entries.reason: Shared Miniflare harness: the HTTP fixture's Durable Object wrapper, re-exported by other fixtures' bundles. Harness code, never part of the shipped Worker bundle.
Platform fakes that stand in for Worker bindings inside fixture bundles. Exists only so fixtures can run; the production bundle uses the real bindings.
The production entry module itself. The fixture boot is its createRoomServer core; loading server.mjs in a fixture would boot a second server (ports, locks, jobs) instead of constructing one.

defaultServerArgs wiring (OAuth configs, env mailer, channel webhook inbox) is assembled by the entry points; the canonical fixture boot passes createRoomServer's defaults so suite boots stay hermetic. Suites that exercise the wired shape import defaultServerArgs directly (tests/channel-inbound-boot.test.js).
Single-instance lock around the on-disk database file. Fixture boots use an in-memory store with no file to lock and no second process to exclude.

The paused (maintenance-mode) handler is an entry-point concern: server.mjs builds a bare node:http server from it without constructing a room server at all. Maintenance boots are covered by tests/maintenance.test.js driving server.mjs itself.

The env-configured magic-link mailer is constructed by defaultServerArgs on the entry path. Fixture boots use the unconfigured mailer so no suite can send real mail; mailer-configured boots are covered where defaultServerArgs is imported.

Boot-time generation of the /docs/agents pages is a Node-entry concern: server.mjs generates any missing generated pages from the committed docs/agents/*.md sources so a self-hosted checkout serves the connection guide llms.txt advertises. Fixture boots construct createRoomServer against their own asset roots and must not write generated pages into a tree.
Digest rendering for the node entry's growth HTTP surface, constructed only by server.mjs. The fixture boot constructs no growth surface (growth: null).
The read-only /growth/* HTTP surface exists only on the node entry; createRoomServer receives it as the `growth` argument, which fixture boots pass as null.
Growth snapshot load/save around the node entry's listen/close lifecycle. No fixture boot persists a growth snapshot.

rules: BG-1 boot-graph census allowlist — the intentional differences between the fixture boot (createRoomServer({ store })) and the production entry boot (server.mjs), and between the canonical Cloudflare fixture bundle and the production Worker bundle. EDIT RULES: every entry names exactly one module (repo-relative path), the side it appears on, the suites it applies to, an owner (the subsystem that constructs or consumes it) and a reason it is intentionally absent from the other boot. An entry whose module stops differing is stale and fails the census — remove it in the same PR that removes the difference. A new difference fails the census until it is either fixed (preferred: the boots converge) or entered here with owner + reason. No globs, no wildcards, no silent entries.
